mainTopic: Conditions in a גט: how strongly רבי's view is shown, binding deadlines, the lost coat, forgiving the payment, the rain-watered field, and payment given against the husband's will.
overview: This amud begins by defending רב יהודה. A ברייתא shows רבי and חכמים arguing about a גט given 'from today and after death,' and the גמרא explains that it chose that case to show how far רבי's lenient view goes, since showing the strength of a lenient view is preferred. Next, the גמרא explains why the משנה must say that a thirty-day deadline is a real condition, and it fills in missing words in the משנה: רבנן and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue about a lost coat, and the story in צידן supports רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. רבי אסי asks what happens if a husband forgives the 200 זוז he made a condition of the גט, and רבי יוחנן rules that she is not divorced. A משנה about vows is brought against him, but the גמרא answers that a husband's condition is meant to burden her, while a vow's condition was only for gain. The same idea settles an argument between רב יוסף and רבה about a sharecropper whose fourth watering was done by rain, and it shows that both can follow רבנן. Finally, רבא learns from הלל's enactment about houses in walled cities that a wife's payment forced on her husband against his will does not fulfill the condition of a גט. His proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא: 'From today and after death'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where חכמים say a גט given 'from today and after my death' is a doubtful גט, and רבי says it is a valid גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: If he said 'from today and after my death,' it is a גט and not a גט. These are the words of חכמים. רבי says: a case like this is a valid גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that shows where רבי and חכמים argue. It is bringing this to show that their argument is about the wording 'from today and after death,' not about 'על מנת.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים are unsure whether the husband meant the גט to work today or only after his death, so the גט is in doubt. רבי holds the גט is fully valid. Because the ברייתא shows the argument in this case, it suggests that everyone agrees about על מנת, and that is hard to fit with רב יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught in a ברייתא (used to bring support or to raise a difficulty)
From today and after [my] death, a two-part wording for when the גט takes effect
It is a גט and not a גט, meaning a doubtful גט
Like this, a case like this

steps.confusionAlert: 'גט ואינו גט' does not mean the גט is half-valid. It means we are unsure whether it works, so the woman is treated strictly both ways.

phrases.english: And it was taught in a ברייתא:
[If he said: This is your גט] 'from today and after [my] death' –
it is a גט and not a גט, these are the words of the Sages;
Rabbi says: [a case] like this is a [valid] גט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of whether על מנת counts as מעכשיו by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי and חכמים argue only about 'from today and after death,' while על מנת works like 'from now' according to everyone.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the argument between חכמים and רבי.

steps.title: Why didn't they argue about על מנת?
steps.stepSummary: According to רב יהודה, who says רבי and רבנן argue about על מנת, the ברייתא should have shown their argument in the על מנת case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב יהודה, who said they argue about 'על מנת': instead of arguing about 'from today and after death,' let them argue about 'על מנת'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה. If the real argument is about על מנת, why does the ברייתא show it in a different case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה placed the disagreement in the על מנת case. A ברייתא would normally record an argument in the case where it actually exists. Showing it only in the 'from today and after death' case looks like the על מנת case is not in dispute.

phrases.english: And according to Rav Yehuda – who said:
they argue about 'on condition,'
rather than arguing about 'from today and after death,'
let them argue about 'on condition'!
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is the standard printed spelling, and the word in square brackets is the corrected one. Both mean 'let them argue.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב יְהוּדָה – דְּאָמַר: בְּ״עַל מְנָת״ פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 1 to challenge רב יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim that רבי and רבנן argue about על מנת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If they really argued about על מנת, the ברייתא should have recorded their argument in that case.

steps.title: To show how far רבי goes
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא chose the 'from today and after death' case to show the strength of רבי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: To tell you the strength of רבי's position.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב יהודה. The ברייתא picked this case on purpose, to show how far רבי's view reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'from today and after death' wording is more doubtful than plain על מנת. Even so, רבי says the גט is fully valid. Showing his view in the harder case teaches us how strong his position is, and he would surely say the same about על מנת.

keyTerms.meaning: His strength, how far his view goes

phrases.english: To inform you of the strength of Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the ברייתא chose this case: to highlight a strong opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the choice of case showed that על מנת is not in dispute.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case was chosen to show how strongly רבי holds that the גט works.

steps.title: Why not show רבנן's strength instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: let them argue about על מנת, and that would show how far רבנן's view goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let them argue about 'על מנת,' and that would tell you the strength of רבנן's position!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. Choosing the על מנת case would also show something strong, this time about רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If they argued about על מנת, we would learn that רבנן hold the גט is doubtful even with that common, milder wording. That would show how far the strict view goes. So why prefer showing רבי's strength over רבנן's?

phrases.english: But let them argue about 'on condition' –
and [that would] inform you of the strength of the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיפַּלְגוּ בְּ״עַל מְנָת״ – וּלְהוֹדִיעֲךָ כֹּחָן דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא wanted to show רבי's strength.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Either case would show someone's strength, so the choice still needs a reason.

steps.title: Showing the strength of a lenient view is better
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא prefers to show how far a lenient (היתר) view goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The strength of a lenient view is preferable to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a final answer. A ברייתא would rather show the strength of a lenient view than a strict one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anyone can be strict when in doubt, so a strict view is not a big חידוש. A lenient view needs confidence, so showing how far it goes teaches more. That is why the ברייתא showed רבי's lenient view in the harder case.

keyTerms.meaning: The strength of a lenient ruling

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה can still say רבי and רבנן argue about על מנת. The ברייתא showed their argument in the 'from today and after death' case only to highlight how far רבי's lenient view reaches.

phrases.english: The strength of leniency is preferable to him.
phrases.notes: 'To him' means to the one who taught the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A general rule about which kind of teaching a ברייתא prefers.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Showing רבנן's strict strength would have been just as good.
steps.terutzMaskana: Showing the strength of a lenient view is preferred.

steps.title: The משנה: give me money within thirty days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about a גט given on condition that she pays him within thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'On condition that you give me [money] from now until thirty days,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה and quotes it. This sets up a question about it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that if she pays within thirty days she is divorced, and if not, she is not. The גמרא quotes only the opening words and relies on the rest being known.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on, the rest of the quote

phrases.english: 'On condition that you give me [money]'
from now until thirty days,' and so on.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתְּנִי לִי מִכָּאן וְעַד שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם״ וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the על מנת discussion and starts a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט given on condition that she pays within thirty days works only if she pays in time.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to teach this, since the condition simply has to be kept.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה for teaching something that seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He set a condition with a deadline. If she didn't meet it, the condition wasn't kept, so of course the גט fails. Why say it?

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for the משנה quoted in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling about the thirty-day condition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A condition that was not kept obviously fails, so the משנה seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: The deadline is a real condition
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought the husband did not truly care about the deadline and only wanted to hurry her. The משנה teaches that the deadline is a real condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that his insistence is not real insistence, and he only came to hurry her along. So it teaches us that it is a real condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה is needed. Without it, we might have treated the thirty days as mere pressure, not a true condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People often set deadlines just to get someone moving, without really meaning that a late payment cancels everything. The משנה teaches that here the deadline counts. If she pays after thirty days, the גט does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: To hurry her, to push her

steps.whatToRemember: When a husband sets a deadline on a condition for a גט, the deadline is binding. We do not assume he only meant to hurry her.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that a time limit inside a condition is taken seriously, and missing it can cancel a גט.

phrases.english: You might have said
his insistence is not [real] insistence –
and he comes [only] to hurry her along;
[therefore] it teaches us [that it is a real condition].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge from step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the mistaken idea the משנה comes to prevent.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The deadline was only meant to hurry her and is not truly part of the condition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The deadline is a real condition, and if she misses it the גט does not take effect.

steps.title: Quoting the story of the incident in צידן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל tells of an incident in צידן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: There was an incident in צידן, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the next line of the משנה so it can ask about it. This step sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's story is about a man who made a גט conditional on getting back his coat, and the coat was lost. The חכמים ruled that she may give him the coat's value. The גמרא only quotes the opening words, because it is about to ask what this story is doing here.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא whose view is quoted in the משנה
An incident; a real case that happened
צידן, the city where the incident took place

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
There was an incident in Tzaidan, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' stands for the rest of the משנה's story: the man whose coat was lost, and the ruling that she pays its value.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּצַיְדָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the thirty-day condition (Steps 6-8) to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In an incident in צידן, when a man made a גט conditional on getting back his coat and the coat was lost, the חכמים ruled that she may give its value.

steps.title: What is this story meant to support?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what earlier teaching the story is meant to back up, since nothing just before it in the משנה is about a coat.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did he teach before, that he now brings a story?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem: a story in a משנה usually backs up a rule stated just before it. Here no such rule appears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous line of the משנה was about paying within thirty days, not about a lost coat or paying the value instead. So the story seems to hang in the air with nothing to support. The גמרא wants to know what rule it is attached to.

keyTerms.meaning: What did he teach? (what rule was stated earlier?)

phrases.english: What did he teach before
that he now brings an incident?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the quoted story fits into the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The way the משנה is put together: the story in Step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A story is brought to support a rule, but no matching rule appears before it in the משנה.

steps.title: The משנה is missing words: the coat argument
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is missing a line. רבנן say a lost coat means the condition fails, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says she pays its value, and the story in צידן supports him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words. This is what it means: If he said to her, 'On condition that you give me my coat,' and the coat was lost, she cannot pay its value, because he said 'my coat' exactly. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: she gives him its value. And רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: There was also an incident in צידן with a man who told his wife, 'This is your גט on condition that you give me my coat,' and the coat was lost, and the חכמים said she should give him its value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that some words are missing from the משנה, and it fills them in. Once the missing argument is added, the story clearly supports רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added line is an argument. רבנן say he asked for this exact coat, so money is not a substitute and the גט fails. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says she may pay its value, and he backs this up with the case in צידן, where the חכמים ruled the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Exactly; specifically this and nothing else

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'my coat exactly' at the start of the filled-in line are the view of רבנן, even though no name is attached. Only after that does רבן שמעון בן גמליאל give his lenient view.
steps.whatToRemember: With a lost coat: רבנן say the condition must be met exactly, so the גט fails. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says paying its value is enough, and he supports this with the case in צידן.

phrases.english: The משנה is missing words,
and this is what it teaches:
If he said to her:
"On condition that you give me my coat,"
and his coat was lost,
he told her 'my coat' exactly.
phrases.notes: So paying money won't do, and the גט fails. This is the view of רבנן.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
She gives him its value.
And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
There was also an incident in Tzaidan,
with a man who said to his wife:
"This is your bill of divorce
on condition that you give me my coat,"
and his coat was lost,
and the Sages said:
She should give him its value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10 by filling in the missing words of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story looked like it had no rule to support.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה left out an argument between רבנן and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about a lost coat, and the story supports רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: רבי אסי asks: what if the husband forgives the money?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי asks רבי יוחנן about a גט given on condition of 200 זוז, after which the husband says the money is forgiven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי asked רבי יוחנן: If a man says, 'This is your גט on condition that you give me 200 זוז,' and then he says to her, 'They are forgiven to you,' what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רבי אסי asks whether forgiving the money counts as meeting the condition, so that the גט works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The condition was that she pays. Once he forgives the money, she will never actually pay. The question is whether his forgiving takes the place of payment, or whether the condition simply was never met.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a real question of law)
They are forgiven to you; you don't have to pay

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַסִּי מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi asked Rabbi Yoḥanan:
"This is your bill of divorce

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתְּנִי לִי מָאתַיִם זוּז״,
phrases.english: on condition that you give me two hundred zuz,"
and then he said to her, "They are forgiven to you,"
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַסִּי מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about conditions in a גט, after the coat argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does forgiving the money count as meeting a payment condition, so that the גט takes effect?

steps.title: The question works in both views
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי אסי's question can be asked both according to רבנן and according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the question be asked according to רבנן; let it be asked according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how wide the question is: it is open according to both sides of the coat argument. This sets up an explanation of why each side could go either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the coat argument already settles this question, with one view leading to one answer and the other view to the other answer. The גמרא says no: the question stays open even within each view. The next lines will explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be asked; the question applies
The Sages (the majority view in the argument)

phrases.english: Let the question be asked according to the Rabbis;
let it be asked according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבָּנַן; תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the scope of רבי אסי's question by linking it to both views in the coat argument from Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Shows that the question does not depend on the argument between רבנן and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל; it is open in both views.

steps.title: Spelling out both sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows why the question works for רבנן and also for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ask it according to רבנן: maybe רבנן only said the condition fails when the husband did not forgive it, but here he said 'it is forgiven.' Or ask it according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: maybe he only allowed the גט because she pays the husband money, but when she gives nothing at all, he would agree it fails.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי אסי's question is open no matter which side of the coat argument you follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן were strict in the coat case, but maybe only because the husband never gave up his claim. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was lenient, but maybe only because the husband still got paid. Forgiving the money completely is a new case that neither opinion clearly covers.

keyTerms.meaning: He forgave or waived it for her

phrases.english: Let it be asked according to the Rabbis:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָתָם,
phrases.english: The Rabbis only said their ruling there
phrases.notes: 'There' means the lost-coat case from step 11, where רבנן said the condition fails.

phrases.english: because he did not forgive it for her;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, הָא קָאָמַר לַהּ: ״מְחוּלִים לָךְ״;
phrases.english: but here, he did say to her: "It is forgiven for you";
Or perhaps,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לָא קָאָמַר,
phrases.english: even Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel only said his ruling
because she satisfies him with money;
but completely, with nothing given, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides that step 13 said the question could be asked on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does forgiving the money count as meeting the condition, under either opinion in the coat case?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules she is not divorced
steps.stepSummary: Forgiving the money does not complete the condition, so the גט does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: She is not divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers רבי אסי's question: saying 'it is forgiven' does not make the גט take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The condition was that she would pay 200 זוז, and she has not paid. Forgiving the debt does not count as payment, so the condition is not met and the גט does not work.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, if a גט depends on her paying money, the husband cannot just forgive the money and treat the condition as met.

phrases.english: He said to him: She is not divorced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question laid out in steps 12 to 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She is not divorced; forgiving the money does not complete the condition.

steps.title: Objection from a vow that can be released by forgiving
steps.stepSummary: A משנה about vows suggests that saying 'it is as if I received it' does count.
steps.simpleTranslation: An objection was raised: Someone says to his friend, 'Benefit from me is forbidden to you by קונם, unless you give my son one כור of wheat and two barrels of wine.' רבי מאיר says the friend is forbidden until he gives. The חכמים say this person can release his own vow without a חכם, by saying, 'I consider it as if I received it.'
steps.whatsHappening: Someone challenges רבי יוחנן's answer using a משנה about a vow with a condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the vow case, the חכמים let the person cancel his condition by saying 'it is as if I got it.' That looks just like a husband saying 'the money is forgiven,' so the גט should work too.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him
A word used to make a vow forbidding something
I consider it as if I received it

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
One who says to his fellow:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in נדרים.

phrases.english: "Benefiting from me is konam for you,
phrases.notes: He means: you are forbidden to get any benefit from me.

phrases.english: if you do not give my son

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹר אֶחָד שֶׁל חִטִּין וּשְׁתֵּי חָבִיּוֹת שֶׁל יַיִן״,
phrases.english: one kor of wheat and two barrels of wine",

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אָסוּר עַד שֶׁיִּתֵּן;
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: It is forbidden until he gives;
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: אַף זֶה – יָכוֹל לְהַתִּיר אֶת נִדְרוֹ
phrases.english: Even this one can release his vow
without a Sage,
and he says: "I consider it as if I have received it"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's ruling from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that forgiving the money does not complete the condition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים let a person treat a condition as met by saying 'as if I received it.' So forgiving the 200 זוז should count too.

steps.title: Why the vow case is different from a גט
steps.stepSummary: A husband's condition is meant to make things hard for her, while the vow's condition was only for a gain he no longer needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, in the גט, the husband meant to make things hard for her, and he has not done that yet. Here, in the vow, he only wanted a gain, and he decided he did not need it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the objection by showing that the two cases have different goals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband who demands 200 זוז wants her to go through the effort of paying. If he forgives it, that goal never happens, so the condition is not met. The man in the vow only wanted a gift for his son, so if he gives it up, nothing he was really after is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: To make things hard for her

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'there' (הָתָם) means the גט case and 'here' (הָכָא) means the vow case. That is the opposite of what you might expect, since the גמרא is mainly discussing the גט.

phrases.english: How can you compare these?!
There, he intends to make things hard for her,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the husband and the גט.

phrases.english: and he has not made things hard for her.
Here, it is for the sake of gain,
and he decided it was not needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 16 and keeps רבי יוחנן's ruling in place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the purpose of the condition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A vow condition and a גט condition work the same, so forgiving should work in both.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גט condition is meant to put her through effort, so forgiving it defeats its purpose. A vow condition was only for gain, so it can be dropped.
steps.whatToRemember: Whether a condition can be forgiven depends on why it was made: to burden her (cannot be forgiven) or for his own gain (can be dropped).

steps.title: Story of a sharecropper promised more for an extra watering
steps.stepSummary: A landowner offers a third of the crop for four waterings, but rain does the fourth watering.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man said to his sharecropper: Everyone waters three times and takes a quarter of the crop. You water four times and take a third. In the end, rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story to set up the next question. The question itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deal tied a bigger share to a fourth watering. Rain did that watering, so the worker never had to do it. This sets up the question of whether he still gets a third.

keyTerms.meaning: Sharecropper who works a field for part of the crop

phrases.english: A certain man said to his sharecropper:
Everyone waters three times,
and they eat a quarter;
phrases.notes: 'Eat' here means taking that share of the crop as pay.

phrases.english: you, water four times,
and eat a third.
In the end, rain came.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case about a condition that becomes unnecessary, after the גט discussion has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet; this sets up a case where the extra work was made unnecessary by rain.

steps.title: Two opinions on the rain-watered field
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the sharecropper did not water, so the condition failed. רבה says the watering was not needed, so the condition counts as done.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: But he did not water it. רבה said: But it was not needed.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give opposite rulings on the case from the last step, where rain did the fourth watering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף looks at the actual act: the worker never did the fourth watering, so he loses the extra pay. רבה looks at the purpose: the field got what it needed, so the worker still earns the third.

keyTerms.meaning: He drew water and watered the field

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
But he did not water it.
phrases.notes: He means the worker never did the fourth watering himself, since the rain did it.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
But it was not needed.
phrases.notes: After the rain, a fourth watering would have been pointless, so the worker should not lose out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף הָא לָא דְּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two rulings on the sharecropper case presented in Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף: the condition was not done, so he gets the regular share. רבה: the condition was not needed, so he gets the third.

steps.title: Is this the same as the earlier argument about conditions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רב יוסף holds like רבנן and רבה holds like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב יוסף ruled like רבנן, and רבה ruled like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to link this new argument to the earlier argument about a גט given on condition. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן said the exact condition must be done, which looks like רב יוסף. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said doing what the condition really wanted is enough, which looks like רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא may reject)

steps.confusionAlert: Words starting with לֵימָא usually bring a suggestion the גמרא is about to push back on. Do not treat it as the final answer.

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav Yosef said it like the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: These are the Rabbis from the earlier case, who say the exact condition must be done.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּה דְּאָמַר כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל?
phrases.english: and Rabba said it like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to tie the two rulings of Step 19 to the earlier argument between the תנאים about the lost coat (Step 11).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the argument between רב יוסף and רבה simply repeat the argument between רבנן and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?

steps.title: That would make the rulings contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows רבה, but in this topic it does not follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so רבה cannot simply hold like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think so? We hold that the הלכה follows רבה, and here the הלכה does not follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion from the last step by showing it leads to a contradiction in the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that the הלכה follows רבה against רב יוסף. If רבה held like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, we would have to rule like him, yet we rule against him here. So the suggestion cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so?
We hold, it is settled for us

phrases.english: And can you really think so?!
But don't we hold that
the halacha follows Rabba;
phrases.notes: This is the general rule when רבה and רב יוסף argue.

phrases.aramaic: וּבְהָא – אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל!
phrases.english: and in this matter, the halacha is not like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the link suggested in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבה holds like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two settled rules (הלכה follows רבה; הלכה is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל here) would clash if רבה held like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Both opinions can follow the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: רבה can hold like רבנן too: רבנן are strict only when the husband wants to make things hard for her, but the landowner only wanted a watered field, and it got that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really both follow רבנן. רב יוסף follows רבנן. And רבה can tell you: I said my ruling even according to רבנן. רבנן were strict there only because the husband meant to make things hard for her. But here the condition was only for his gain, and that watering was not needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that רבה does not need רבן שמעון בן גמליאל at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן insisted on the exact condition in the גט case because the husband wanted her to go through some hardship. The landowner had no such goal; he only wanted his field watered for a better crop. Once rain did that, there is no reason to hold the worker to the exact act.

keyTerms.meaning: They only said it in that case
To make things hard for her

steps.whatToRemember: Both רב יוסף and רבה hold like רבנן. The difference is the purpose of the condition: a condition meant to make things hard must be done exactly, but a condition meant only for gain is met once the gain is there.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the same idea as Step 17. Whether a condition must be kept word for word depends on why it was made.

phrases.english: Rather, really it is like the Rabbis.
Rav Yosef is like the Rabbis;
and Rabba could say to you:
I said it even according to the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָתָם –
phrases.english: the Rabbis only said it there
phrases.notes: "There" is the earlier גט case, where the wife had to hand back a specific item.

phrases.english: because he meant to make things hard for her;
but here, it is only for the sake of gain,
and this was not needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 21 by placing both opinions within רבנן's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the purpose of the condition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה needs רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's lenient view to say the condition was met.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה fits רבנן too, because רבנן's strictness applies only when the condition was meant to make things hard, not when it was only for gain.

steps.title: הלל's enactment for redeeming a house in a walled city
steps.stepSummary: A משנה describes how buyers hid to stop sellers from buying back their house, and how הלל הזקן let the seller deposit the money in the Temple chamber instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned elsewhere: at first, the buyer would hide on the last day of the twelve months so the house would become permanently his. הלל הזקן enacted that the seller may deposit his money in the chamber, break the door, and go in. Whenever the buyer wants, he can come and take his money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה about houses in walled cities. This is background that sets up רבא's lesson in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A seller of a house in a walled city can buy it back only within twelve months; after that it belongs to the buyer forever. Buyers abused this by hiding so no one could pay them. הלל הזקן made the money count as paid even without the buyer taking it.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned elsewhere, in a משנה from another place
He enacted, made a rabbinic rule

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in ערכין about a house sold inside a walled city (ויקרא 25:29–30).

phrases.english: At first, he would hide
on the last day of the twelve months,
so that it would be permanently his.
phrases.notes: The one hiding is the buyer, and it means the house. Once the year ends, the seller can't buy it back.

phrases.english: Hillel the Elder enacted
that he may deposit his money in the chamber,
and break the door and enter.
And whenever that one wants,
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the buyer who was hiding.

phrases.english: he may come and take his money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the rain-watering discussion. It brings a source that will teach something about conditions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלל enacted that the seller may deposit the redemption money in the Temple chamber and take back his house, even without the buyer's cooperation.

steps.title: רבא: a conditional גט needs payment with the husband's consent
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from הלל's enactment that if a גט depends on her giving him 200 זוז, she is divorced only if she gives it with his consent.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: from הלל's enactment we learn that if a husband says, 'Here is your גט on condition that you give me two hundred זוז,' and she gave it with his consent, she is divorced. If she gave it against his will, she is not divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא states a rule about a conditional גט and says it comes from הלל's enactment. The next step shows how he gets it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The condition is 'giving' money. רבא rules that forcing money on an unwilling husband does not count as giving. So the condition is not met and the גט does not take effect.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up whose consent matters. Here it is the husband, the one receiving the money, who must agree to take it.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
From Hillel's enactment we can learn:
"This is your bill of divorce

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתְּנִי לִי מָאתַיִם זוּז״,
phrases.english: on condition that you give me two hundred zuz,"
and she gave it to him with his consent, she is divorced;
against his will, she is not divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: מִתַּקָּנָתוֹ שֶׁל הִלֵּל נִשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה just quoted as the source for a new rule about a conditional גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט given on condition that she pay him takes effect only if she pays with his consent, not if she forces the money on him.

steps.title: Why הלל's enactment proves רבא's rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that since הלל needed a special enactment to make forced giving count, forced giving must not count normally.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since הלל needed to enact that giving against the receiver's will counts as giving,
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins to show how he learns his rule from הלל. The sentence continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If forced giving already counted, הלל would not have needed an enactment. The fact that he needed one shows that, by the basic law, giving against someone's will is not real giving. That is why the wife's forced payment does not fulfill the condition.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic way the גמרא learns: if a special rule was needed, then without it the law must be the opposite.

phrases.english: Since Hillel needed
to enact that giving against his will
phrases.notes: 'His will' means the buyer, who did not want to take the money.

phrases.english: counts as giving,

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּאִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ לְהִלֵּל לְתַקּוֹנֵי נְתִינָה בְּעַל כּוּרְחֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבא learns his rule from הלל's enactment.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that a wife's payment against her husband's will does not fulfill the condition of the גט
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that הלל needed a special enactment to make forced giving count in the walled-city house case
